category.main_topic: He refuses a comfortable class because students who delayed are now asking for extensions
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Defend pace and strictness with a current example
category.core_message: A pleasant class would betray the goal of selection. He cites extension requests as evidence that a short, late preparation is not working.
category.narrative_structure: accept dislike, describe the easy class he will not run, then the mails
category.hook: Dislike me now if you want
category.takeaway: The three-month window is the point of the warning
category.rationale: Part pedagogy, part account of his own course.

transcript.original_text: आप मुझे नापसंद कर लो अभी। यू कैन [संगीत] फील दैट आई एम ओवरली स्ट्रिक्ट टू फास्ट। आई टीच बल्कि कंटेंट। मैं बहुत ज्यादा पढ़ाता हूं। आप [संगीत] कुछ भी फील कर लो। आई एम नॉट गोइंग टू लाई टू यू। एंड आई एम नॉट गोइंग टू वायलेट योर ट्रस्ट जो आपने ओरिजिनली मेरे पे रखा था। टू गेट यू सिलेक्टेड। [संगीत] आई कैन मेक यू फील वेरी गुड। कि यार इकोनॉमिक सर्वे नेक्स्ट ईयर आएगा। इकॉनमी नेक्स्ट ईयर देखते हैं। रोज एक टॉपिक पढ़ते हैं। शैलो कंटेंट [संगीत] पढ़ लेते हैं। मैं आपको ही कह देता हूं पॉइंट्स बताओ। फिर आप कुछ-कुछ पॉइंट्स बता देना। थोड़े बहुत मैं बोर्ड पर लिख दूंगा। थोड़ी बहुत यू नो बातें कर लेते हैं कि देखो अरे लवासना में ऐसे होता है। इस [संगीत] टीशर्ट में ये टीशर्ट मेरे को एनपीए में ऐसे मिली वगैरह और मैं चला जाऊं। आप भी खुश मैं भी खुश होगा क्या उससे? अभी पता है इस साल जिन लोगों ने मेंस दिया है और उन्होंने इन्हीं दो मंथ्स में प्रिपरेशन करी है उनके मेल्स आ रहे हैं मुझे। क्यों मेल्स आ रहे हैं पता है कि सर हमारी एमएमटी जो हमने लिया था ना 2026 के लिए उसको एक्सटेंड कर दो [संगीत] प्लीज। क्योंकि नहीं हो पाती इस टाइम में प्रिपरेशन यार जिसने इस टाइम पे मैं क्यों कह रहा था यह 3 मंथ्स बहुत रेलेवेंट है। जिसने इन तीन महीनों में पढ़ाई नहीं करी उसका नहीं हो रहा मी मेंस अगले साल।
transcript.english_translation: Go ahead and dislike me right now. You can feel that I am overly strict, too fast. I teach a lot of content. I teach a great deal. Feel whatever you want. I am not going to lie to you. And I am not going to violate the trust you originally placed in me, to get you selected. I can make you feel very good. That the Economic Survey will come next year, we'll see Economy next year, we read one topic a day, we read shallow content. I can tell you to state points, then you state some points, I write a little on the board, we chat a bit — look, this is how it is in LBSNAA, I got this T-shirt in the NPA, and so on — and I leave. You will be happy, I will be happy. What will come of that? Right now, the people who wrote Mains this year and who prepared in just these two months are mailing me. Do you know why the mails are coming? Sir, please extend the MMT we had taken for 2026. Because preparation cannot get done in this time. Why was I saying that these three months are very relevant? The person who did not study in these three months is not managing Mains next year. [Names and the product acronym are as captioned. Some sentences are compressed.]

metadata.description: Motivation is not enough for success

category.main_topic: Enthusiasm and motivation fade; hard thinking is the requirement
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Separate motivation from the work
category.core_message: Most people do not even attend everything. Achievement is tied to hard work and questioning one's thinking.
category.narrative_structure: evidence offer, then the requirement
category.hook: He offers to show an attendance graph
category.takeaway: Motivation at the start is not the work
category.rationale: Short and general. The graph itself is only offered, not described numerically.

transcript.english_translation: I can even bring the attendance graph and show you here. Most people don't even attend all the classes. At the start, in the beginning itself, enthusiasm is high. This is not easy to do. This will require you to really work on your thinking, to question your mind, to question your critical thinking, and work really hard. It is only when you work hard that you will be able to achieve this. I hope this is clear to everyone. [The caption ends there.]

category.main_topic: Integrated farming as a circular system with no waste
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Define the concept through one farm loop
category.core_message: Outputs of one activity become inputs of the next, which is why he connects it to the circular economy.
category.narrative_structure: definition, then a loop of examples
category.hook: There is no waste on the farm
category.takeaway: Use every leftover as an input

transcript.original_text: हम कहते हैं कि कोई वेस्ट है ही नहीं फार्म में। इंटीग्रेटेड फार्मिंग सिस्टम इज कनेक्टेड टू अ वेरी मेजर कांसेप्ट दैट इज इन द न्यूज़ राइट नाउ कॉल्ड सर्कुलर इकॉनमी। कि यार ये आपने वीट उगाया। सीड्स तो आप मार्केट में बेचोगे। जो चाफ बचा है इससे आप पिग्स का पाउडर बना दो। पिग्स जो वेस्ट प्रोड्यूस कर रहे हैं इससे आप वीट प्लांट के लिए मनोर बना दो। ट्रीज आप ऐसी जगह लगाओ ताकि वो पिग्स को शेड प्रोवाइड कर सके। जो पोंड में वेस्ट वाटर है उससे आप पिग्स को नहला सकते हो। है ना? आपको बिल्कुल क्लीन वाटर तो नहीं चाहिए। और जो आपके पास ये वीट का बचा हुआ वेस्ट है उससे आप फिशेस का भी पाउडर बना सकते हो। सो देयर इज नो वेस्ट इन योर फार्म। व्हाटएवर इज वेस्ट यू नीड टू यूटिलाइज इट। दिस इज मीनिंग ऑफ इंटीग्रेटेड फार्मिंग सिस्टम।
transcript.english_translation: We say there is no waste at all on a farm. An integrated farming system is connected to a very major concept that is in the news right now, called the circular economy. You grew wheat. You will sell the seeds in the market. From the chaff that is left, you make powder for the pigs. From the waste the pigs produce, you make manure for the wheat plant. Plant trees in such a place that they can provide shade to the pigs. With the waste water in the pond you can bathe the pigs. Right? You don't need completely clean water. And from this leftover wheat waste you have, you can also make powder for the fishes. So there is no waste on your farm. Whatever is waste, you need to utilise it. This is the meaning of an integrated farming system. [The caption says 'manure' in a phonetic form and 'mind' is not used. One word was heard as manure.]

category.main_topic: Why GST changed which states received tax, and what the compensation cess was for
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Explain GST versus VAT through the state complaint
category.core_message: VAT-plus-excise followed production. GST follows consumption, so producing states feared a shortfall, and a compensation cess was introduced.
category.narrative_structure: complaint, contrast, remedy
category.hook: Some states complained when GST arrived
category.takeaway: The cess is explained as cover for industrial states' shortfall
category.entities: GST; VAT; excise; Haryana; compensation cess
category.rationale: The speech is a concept comparison.

transcript.original_text: So when GST was introduced, some states had a complaint. Um, GST is consumption based tax. I mean I consume in Haryana, I consume there, so the tax goes there. I'm paying central GST to central government and state GST to Haryana government. Before that we had VAT system, VAT plus excise system was actually a production based tax. So the tax goes to the state where the production happens. So earlier we had a production based system, now we have a consumption based system. So when GST was implemented uh there were many states that said that we are industrial states because we are industrial states. Because a lot of production is happening in our states. We were getting a lot of taxes. We were getting a lot of taxes. Now you have made it a consumption based tax. So I will have a tax shortfall. This was the states' problem, especially of those states that were industrial states. So government introduced a compensation to states cess. This will cover the shortfall of industrial states. We will pay for the shortfall of states with this GST compensation cess.
transcript.english_translation: So when GST was introduced, some states had a complaint. GST is a consumption-based tax. I mean, I consume in Haryana, I consume there, so the tax goes there. I'm paying central GST to the central government and state GST to the Haryana government. Before that we had the VAT system. VAT plus excise was actually a production-based tax. So the tax goes to the state where the production happens. So earlier we had a production-based system, now we have a consumption-based system. So when GST was implemented, there were many states that said that we are industrial states. Because a lot of production is happening in our states, we were getting a lot of taxes. Now you have made it a consumption-based tax, so I will have a tax shortfall. This was the states' problem, especially of those states that were industrial states. So the government introduced a compensation-to-states cess. This will cover the shortfall of industrial states. We will pay for the shortfall of states with this GST compensation cess. [This track is English.]

category.main_topic: Weak manufacturing and the preference for foreign-branded goods
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Connect brand preference to the import bill
category.core_message: If domestic goods are not wanted or not available, spending goes to foreign goods and imports rise.
category.narrative_structure: brand example, missing products, then the macro result
category.hook: Would you buy the shirt if the brand had an obviously local name?
category.takeaway: He says imports rise because Indian manufactured goods are not good enough
category.entities: Peter England; Suresh Lucknow, a hypothetical name
category.rationale: A concept argument, not a news item.

transcript.original_text: पीटर इंग्लैंड एक ऐसी कंपनी है जो एक्चुअली इंडियन है। बट अगर इसका नाम सुरेश लखनऊ होता तो क्या आप इसकी शर्ट खरीदते? पीटर इंग्लैंड की शर्ट तो खरीदनी है। सुरेश लखनऊ इज एन इंडियन नेम। सुरेश लखनऊ नाम होता तो आप खरीदते। नहीं आपको फोन खरीदना है। आप बोलते हो मुझे इंडियन कंपनी का फोन खरीदना है। है ही नहीं इंडियन कंपनी। आप वॉच खरीदते हो। आप बोलते हो मुझे इंडियन मेड वॉच खरीदनी है। नहीं। लोग पैसा खर्च करना चाह रहे हैं। आपके पास मैन्युफैक्चरिंग सेक्टर अच्छा नहीं है। अच्छी प्रोडक्शन नहीं हो रही तो लोग पैसा कहां खर्च करेंगे? क्या वो इंडियन गुड्स खरीदेंगे? नहीं। वो फॉरेन गुड्स खरीदेंगे। तो जब वह फॉरेन गुड्स खरीदेंगे तो क्या होगा? इंपोर्ट्स विल इंक्रीस। यही हो रहा है इंडियन इकॉनमी में। इंपोर्ट्स आर इंक्रीजिंग कॉन्सेंटली। क्योंकि इंडियन मैन्युफैक्चरिंग गुड्स अच्छे हैं ही नहीं। इंडियन मेड गुड्स अच्छे हैं ही
transcript.english_translation: Peter England is a company that is actually Indian. But if its name were Suresh Lucknow, would you buy its shirt? You do want to buy a Peter England shirt. Suresh Lucknow is an Indian name. If the name were Suresh Lucknow, would you buy it? You want to buy a phone. You say, I want to buy a phone from an Indian company. There is no Indian company. You buy a watch. You say, I want to buy an Indian-made watch. No. People want to spend money. You don't have a good manufacturing sector. If good production is not happening, where will people spend money? Will they buy Indian goods? No. They will buy foreign goods. So when they buy foreign goods, what will happen? Imports will increase. This is what is happening in the Indian economy. Imports are increasing constantly, because Indian manufactured goods are just not good. Indian-made goods are just not good. [The caption repeats the last claim and ends mid-phrase. The claim that there is no Indian phone company is the speaker's, as captioned.]

metadata.title: The Real Reason Behind Neem Coated Urea
metadata.user_topic_description: (REAL REASON BETWEEN NEEM COATED UREA)
metadata.description: The Real Reason Behind Neem Coated Urea

category.main_topic: Neem-coated urea as a way to stop subsidy diversion
subtopics: industry cannot use the coated product
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Explain a scheme through the cheat it blocks
category.core_message: Subsidised urea was being diverted to industry. Coating it with neem is said to improve farm use and make industrial use pointless.
category.narrative_structure: the loophole, then the fix
category.hook: A factory owner should not get the farmer subsidy
category.takeaway: Neem coating is the mechanism against diversion
category.rationale: The prices are the speaker's round figures.

transcript.original_text: यू शुड नॉट गेट सब्सिडी इफ यू अ फैक्ट्री ओनर। आपके लिए थोड़ी बनी थी सब्सिडी। गवर्नमेंट ने कहा यूरिया यूज़ होता है दो पर्पस से। एक तो फार्म में यूज़ होता है और एक लेट से इंडस्ट्रीज में यूज़ होता है। तो अगर आप फार्मर हो तो हम यूरिया आपको दे देंगे सब्सिडाइज्ड रेट पे। मार्केट में यूरिया मिलता है ₹1000 का और आपको ₹200 में यूरिया मिल जाएगा। लेकिन अगर आप इंडस्ट्रियलिस्ट हो और आप इंडस्ट्री में यूरिया यूज़ कर रहे हो तो आपको ₹1000 का ही मिलेगा। मैं कहता हूं यार मेरे से ₹400 ले लो और अपना यूरिया मुझे बेच दो। आपको ₹200 में जाके खरीदो और मैं आपको 400 देता हूं। आपका तो 200 का फायदा हो गया। यह वाला यूरिया मुझे दे दो। यूरिया तो सेम ही है। मेरे बिज़नेस का प्रॉफिट बढ़ जाएगा। मल्टीपल गवर्नमेंट्स अक्रॉस द इयर्स हैव टेकन वेरी गुड स्टेप्स टू सॉल्व दिस फर्टिलाइजर प्रॉब्लम। हम यूरिया के ऊपर नीम की कोटिंग कर देते हैं। अब नीम कोटिंग से दो तीन चीजें होती हैं। पहले तो आप नीम कोटेड अगर यूरिया है तो आप उसको फार्म में यूज़ करोगे तो बेटर यूटिलाइज होता है। सेकंडली अगर वो नीम कोटेड है तो उसे इंडस्ट्री में यूज़ कर ही नहीं सकते। क्योंकि इंडस्ट्री में तो नीम का कोई पॉइंट ही नहीं है ना। और नीम की कोटिंग हटा तो पाओगे नहीं आप। तो नीम कोटिंग ऑफ यूरिया कर देते हैं। ना डायवर्जन होगी और एग्रीकल्चर यूज़ भी बेटर होगा।
transcript.english_translation: You should not get the subsidy if you are a factory owner. The subsidy was made, in a sense, for you the farmer. The government said urea is used for two purposes. One, it is used on the farm, and one, it is used in industry. So if you are a farmer, we will give you urea at a subsidised rate. In the market urea is available for 1,000 rupees, and you will get urea for 200 rupees. But if you are an industrialist and you are using urea in industry, you will get it only at 1,000 rupees. I say, take 400 rupees from me and sell me your urea. You buy it for 200 and I give you 400. You made a profit of 200. Give this urea to me. Urea is the same. My business's profit will increase. Multiple governments across the years have taken very good steps to solve this fertiliser problem. We put a neem coating on urea. Now two or three things happen because of neem coating. First, if urea is neem-coated and you use it on the farm, it is utilised better. Second, if it is neem-coated, it cannot be used in industry, because neem has no point in industry, right? And you will not be able to remove the neem coating. So they do neem coating of urea. There will be no diversion, and agricultural use will also be better.

teacher_visibility.method: 59 one-fps frames, sec_001 at 0s through sec_059 at 58s. Hidden samples: 4, 5, 9, 38, 43, 44, 45. The 57s sample is the logo with the teacher absent and is not included in the hidden count. The 58s sample is the poster, counted as with-overlay because his face is visible under the banners. Grayscale opening frames and karaoke lines were not counted as an overlay. Title and logo above the card were not counted as an overlay.
teacher_visibility.counting_note: A frame can show the teacher and an overlay together. Those frames are counted as visible_with_overlay, not as replacement. Percentages are of sampled 1fps frames, not of decoded 30fps frames. If frames_accounted is below sampled_frames, the three buckets do not partition the sample and the percentages are incomplete.

shorts.style_interpretation: Observed template family: rounded_card_karaoke_endslate. Title as read: The Real Reason Behind Neem-Coated Urea. The 1fps sample counted 50 primary-teacher frames, 1 overlay frames, and 7 frames where B-roll hid the teacher, out of 59 sampled frames. These counts describe the sample. They are not a claim about the editor's intention. Direct observations are the timeline rows. Any reason a B-roll insert was chosen is a hypothesis tied to the spoken phrase in that row.
additional_observations: Cut times inside each one-second gap are not pinned finer than the samples. Scene-detect stamps 57.182 and 58.392 were not used to override the 57s logo and 58s poster samples.
The tractor, factory, and pellet inserts may be held stills. Only the field shot holds for three samples. 1 fps does not prove motion.
Most karaoke lines and the rupee diagram were read from the contact sheet. Only the five lines listed above were checked on a full frame.
Board words other than Fertilizer, Eco, usage, pollution, and the later Neem coat circle are [unclear].
The caption track uses 'लेट से इंडस्ट्रीज'; the pixels do not show that phrase written out.
A thin icon strip on the card edge in some teacher samples is [unclear].

category.main_topic: A visit to an Amul factory as evidence of a cooperative's scale
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Use a personal visit to illustrate cooperative success
category.core_message: He presents the factory's research and production scale as a major success of cooperatives.
category.narrative_structure: the academy trip, then the factory
category.hook: Before Kevadia, the batch visits an Amul factory
category.takeaway: He calls the operation world-leading and a cooperative success
category.entities: LBSNAA; Kevadia; Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; Amul; Prime Minister
category.rationale: A fact-and-anecdote short, distinct from the broken origin story in SHORT_37.

transcript.original_text: जब आप भी लबासना जाएंगे लवासना में जब हम खत्म होने वाला होता है फाउंडेशन कोर्स तो आपको लेके जाते हैं सरदार वल्लभ भाई पटेल का जो स्टैचू है केवड़िया में वहां तो आप गुजरात जाते हो फिर केवड़िया जाते हो वहां ऑनरेबल प्राइम मिनिस्टर आते हैं एंड ही एड्रेसेस द न्यू बैच हमें भी एड्रेस किया था वहां पर बट केवड़िया जाने से पहले आई थिंक एवरीवन है टेकन एटलीस्ट वंस टू विजिट वन और द अदर अमूल फैक्ट्री और मैं आपको बता रहा हूं वहां जाके आई वास सो अमेज्ड जिस लेवल पर रिसर्च चल रही है जिस लेवल पे जितनी बड़ी-बड़ी वहां पर फैक्ट्रीज हैं जिस लेवल पर प्रोडक्शन चल रही है वी आर आर वर्ल्ड लीडर्स इन दैट केस। वहां पर रोज मिल्क पाउडर, मिल्क प्रोडक्ट्स इस लेवल पर बन रहे हैं कि आपको लगेगा कि किस लेवल का इंडस्ट्रियल ऑपरेशन है। यू विल बी सरप्राइज टू। आई वास टू सी द लेवल ऑफ इंडस्ट्रियल ऑपरेशन। यहां से अब वो वहां ग्रो करके पहुंच गया। दिस इज़ वन ऑफ द मेजर सक्सेस ऑफ कोऑपरेटर्स इन द कंट्री।
transcript.english_translation: When you too go to LBSNAA — when our foundation course is about to end, they take you to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's statue at Kevadia — so you go to Gujarat, then you go to Kevadia. The honourable Prime Minister comes there and he addresses the new batch. He addressed us there too. But before going to Kevadia, I think everyone is taken at least once to visit one or another Amul factory. And I am telling you, when I went there I was so amazed at the level at which research is going on, the level of how big the factories are there, the level at which production is going on. We are world leaders in that case. Milk powder and milk products are being made there every day at such a level that you will feel, what a level of industrial operation this is. You will be surprised to see the level of industrial operation. I was too. From here it has now grown and reached there. This is one of the major successes of cooperatives in the country. [LBSNAA is again written phonetically in the caption.]

category.main_topic: People drop free material they do not value
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Explain a behavior with his own view counts
category.core_message: Free distribution is associated, in his examples, with not starting or not continuing.
category.narrative_structure: rule, two examples
category.hook: When something is free it is not valued
category.takeaway: A large share of viewers leave between lecture one and lecture three
category.entities: YouTube science and tech lectures; 7 lakh; 2 lakh
category.rationale: The view counts are his claims.

transcript.original_text: व्हेन समथिंग इज़ फ्री, व्हेन समथिंग इज़ फ्री, व्हेन इट इज़ गिवन आउट जस्ट फॉर फ्री। इट इज़ नॉट वैल्यूड। इंश्योरेंस आप फ्री देके देख लो। लोग लेंगे ही नहीं। या उसकी वैल्यू नहीं करेंगे। गिव अनदर एग्जांपल। YouTube पे मेरे सार्थ के चैनल पे मेरे साइंस एंड टेक के सारे लेक्चर हैं। फर्स्ट वीडियो पे तो हैं 7 लाख व्यूज। 7 लाख। मतलब 7 लाख स्टूडेंट्स स्टार्टेड वाचिंग। और थर्ड वीडियो पे बच जाते हैं 2 लाख व्यूज। तो 5 लाख बच्चे ड्रॉप ऑफ कर गए विद इन टू लेक्चर्स। क्यों? मैं फ्री था। देख लिया, छोड़ दिया। हम ड्रॉप ऑफ रेट्स यहां भी देखते हैं। लाइक इवन इन आवर लेक्चर्स, वी सी हाउ मच अटेंडेंस इज़ देयर, हाउ मच ड्रॉप ऑफ रेट्स इज़ देयर। नहीं होता ड्रॉप ऑफ। है ना?
transcript.english_translation: When something is free, when something is free, when it is given out just for free, it is not valued. Try giving insurance for free. People will not even take it, or they will not value it. I'll give another example. On my Science and Tech channel on YouTube, all my science and technology lectures are there. The first video has 7 lakh views. 7 lakh. Meaning 7 lakh students started watching. And by the third video, 2 lakh views are left. So 5 lakh students dropped off within two lectures. Why? I was free. They watched, they left. We see dropout rates here too. Like even in our lectures, we see how much attendance there is, how much the dropout rate is. The dropout does not happen. Right? [The last contrast, paid or live lectures versus free video, is implied but the caption does not name the paid product.]

transcript.original_text: के भी हेड प्राइम मिनिस्टर हैं। ये जो पांच लोग हैं होम मिनिस्टर, डिफेंस मिनिस्टर, फाइनेंस मिनिस्टर और एक्सटर्नल अफेयर्स मिनिस्टर। राइट? ये पांच लोग कैबिनेट कमिटी ऑफ़ सिक्योरिटी में हैं। एंड दीज़ फाइव पीपल आर टेकिंग द बिगेस्ट डिसीजंस। इसके नीचे आता है नेशनल सिक्योरिटी एडवाइजर जो अभी कौन है? अजीत डोबाल सर। है ना? नेशनल सिक्योरिटी एडवाइजर इज हेड ऑफ नेशनल सिक्योरिटी काउंसिल। यह जो आईडिया है यहां पर अब ब्यूरोक्रेटिक स्ट्रक्चर आता है। इनके नीचे एडिशनल एनएसए हैं। एडिशनल एनएसए के नीचे एक मिलिट्री एडवाइजर हैं। तीन डेपुटी एनएसए हैं और नेशनल मैरिटाइम सिक्योरिटी कोऑर्डिनेटर हैं। यह आपको ब्रॉडली पता होना चाहिए।
transcript.english_translation: [The caption starts mid-sentence.] The head is also the Prime Minister. These five people are the Home Minister, the Defence Minister, the Finance Minister, and the External Affairs Minister. Right? These five people are in the Cabinet Committee on Security. And these five people are taking the biggest decisions. Below this comes the National Security Advisor. Who is it right now? Ajit Doval sir. Right? The National Security Advisor is the head of the National Security Council. This idea — here the bureaucratic structure comes in. Below them there are Additional NSAs. Below the Additional NSA there is a Military Advisor. There are three Deputy NSAs, and there is a National Maritime Security Coordinator. You should broadly know this.

metadata.title: Why Does Punjab Have a “Cancer Train”? |
metadata.user_topic_description: (WHY SO MANY CANCER PATIENTS IN PUNJAB)

category.main_topic: Why a train from Punjab is called a cancer train
subtopics: tertiary hospitals in Delhi and Haryana
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Explain a named social fact
category.core_message: High case numbers and travel to tertiary centres produced the popular name. He also separates treatment from cure.
category.narrative_structure: name, cause, terminology distinction
category.hook: A cancer train runs from Punjab
category.takeaway: The name comes from patients travelling for treatment
category.rationale: A current-affairs explainer. No cause of the cancer rate is stated in this caption.

transcript.original_text: कैंसर ट्रेन चलती है पंजाब [संगीत] से। पंजाब में कैंसर के जो केसेस हैं वो बहुत ज्यादा है। तो वहां के जो लोग हैं वो ट्रेंस लेके टर्शरी हॉस्पिटल्स में आते हैं इन दिल्ली एंड हरियाणा फॉर कैंसर ट्रीटमेंट। और ऐसी ट्रेन की ट्रेन आती है कैंसर पेशेंट्स की। क्योंकि कैंसर पेशेंट्स में क्या होता है कि यू कांट क्योर इट। लाइक इट्स वेरी डिफिकल्ट टू से कि आपके कैंसर को हमने क्योर कर दिया। यू कैन ट्रीट इट। देयर आर टू डिफरेंट टर्म्स। तो पंजाब से ट्रेन की ट्रेन चलती हैं। जहां पीपल वुड कम टू टर्शरी हॉस्पिटल्स ऑफ़ दिल्ली फॉर कैंसर ट्रीटमेंट। राइट? एंड दीज़ आर कॉल्ड वेरी फेमसली कैंसर ट्रेंस। वहां पर भी कुछ कैंसर सेंटर्स गवर्नमेंट ने बनाए हैं। तो लोग ट्रेन की ट्रेन में बैठ के उन कैंसर सेंटर्स तक आते हैं। तो इसे कैंसर ट्रेन कहा जाता है।
transcript.english_translation: A cancer train runs from Punjab. The cancer cases in Punjab are very high. So the people there take trains to tertiary hospitals in Delhi and Haryana for cancer treatment. And train after train of cancer patients comes. Because what happens with cancer patients is that you can't cure it. Like, it is very difficult to say that we have cured your cancer. You can treat it. There are two different terms. So train after train runs from Punjab, where people would come to tertiary hospitals of Delhi for cancer treatment. Right? And these are very famously called cancer trains. The government has also made some cancer centres there. So people come sitting in train after train to those cancer centres. So it is called a cancer train.

metadata.title: Forget Globalisation, Nationalism Is Back
metadata.user_topic_description: (RISE OF SOVEREING NATIONALISM)
metadata.description:
Forget Globalisation, Nationalism Is Back |

This video is about the growing trend of sovereign nationalism as countries across the world increasingly prioritize the “Nation First” principle.

category.main_topic: Examples he groups under a return of nationalism
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Argue that countries are putting themselves first
category.core_message: He lines up China, India, and the EU, then a stalled WTO, as signs that countries now prioritise themselves.
category.narrative_structure: three country examples, then an institution
category.hook: China will not export even pandas
category.takeaway: The title's claim is that nationalism is back; the speech supplies examples
category.entities: China; Atmanirbhar Bharat; European Union; WTO Appellate Body; G20; BRICS
category.rationale: An IR explainer built from examples.

transcript.original_text: चाइना में क्या हो रहा है? पंडास तक एक्सपोर्ट करने से चाइना ने मना कर दिया है। हम अपनी टेक्नोलॉजी शेयर नहीं करेंगे। माय कंट्री फर्स्ट। इंडिया क्या बोल रहा है? इंडिया बोल रहा है आत्मनिर्भर भारत। ईयू क्या बोल रहा है? ईयूस न्यू एजेंडा ऑफ स्ट्रेटेजिक ऑटोनमी। अब ईयू भी स्ट्रेटेजिक ऑटोनमी की बात कर रहा है। ग्लोबल लेवल पे क्या हो रहा है? 7 साल से डब्ल्यूटीओ में अपेलेट बॉडी ही नहीं है। फर्क ही नहीं पड़ रहा लोगों को। क्योंकि G20 है क्योंकि ब्रिक्स है। वहां हो जाते हैं डिस्प्यूट्स रिॉल्व। अगर होने होते हैं तो। और नहीं होने होते तो फिर नहीं होते। बिकॉज़ नाउ नोबडी केयर्स। एवरीबडी केयर्स अबाउट दिस नाउ।
transcript.english_translation: What is happening in China? China has refused to export even pandas. We will not share our technology. My country first. What is India saying? India is saying Atmanirbhar Bharat. What is the EU saying? The EU's new agenda of strategic autonomy. Now the EU is also talking about strategic autonomy. What is happening at the global level? For seven years there has been no Appellate Body in the WTO. It makes no difference to people. Because there is the G20, because there is BRICS. Disputes get resolved there, if they are going to be resolved. And if they are not going to be resolved, then they don't. Because now nobody cares. Everybody cares about this now. [The last two sentences point in opposite directions and are both in the caption.]

metadata.title: Are you too just waiting for panic
metadata.user_topic_description: (U R NOT LAZY U R JUST WAITING FOR PANIC TO STUDY)

category.main_topic: Studying only when panic arrives
subtopics: four hours now versus peak productivity a week before Prelims
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Name the pattern of waiting for the exam to get close
category.core_message: The external deadline, not a stable habit, is what produces the long study hours.
category.narrative_structure: hypothetical, examples, then the present slump
category.hook: You would be motivated if Prelims were close
category.takeaway: The productivity peak comes from panic, and it is not here yet
category.rationale: Matches the supplied topic line.

transcript.original_text: अगर यह मंथ ऑफ़ जनवरी होता और आपको मैं कहता प्रीलिम्स के लिए पढ़ना है तो आप लोग सेल्फ मोटिवेटेड होते। इट्स द ब्रूटल ट्रुथ ऑफ़ द मैटर कि जब हमारे पास एक एक्सटर्नल मोटिवेटर होता है ना जब हमें पता होता है कि यार दो दिन बाद एग्जाम है तो हम अपने आप पढ़ लेते हैं। नहीं मन होता तब भी पढ़ लेते हैं। खराब लग रहा होता है तब भी पढ़ लेते हैं। तबीयत खराब होती है तब भी पढ़ लेते हैं। भाई की शादी होती है तब भी पढ़ लेते हैं। क्यों? क्योंकि हमें पता होता है कि यार एग्जाम है। प्रीलिम्स आएगा एक महीने पहले आप पढ़ाई कर ही लोगे। बट प्रीलिम्स के एक दिन पहले एक हफ्ता पहले आपकी प्रोडक्टिविटी एकदम यू नो इट विल बी एट इट स्पीक और अभी हो सकता है आप चारप घंटे पढ़ने में भी स्ट्रगल करो।
transcript.english_translation: If this were the month of January and I told you that you have to study for Prelims, you people would be self-motivated. It's the brutal truth of the matter that when we have an external motivator, when we know that the exam is two days away, then we study on our own. Even when we don't feel like it, we study. Even when we feel awful, we study. Even when we are unwell, we study. Even when our brother is getting married, we study. Why? Because we know that the exam is there. One month before Prelims arrives, you will study anyway. But one day before Prelims, one week before, your productivity will suddenly, you know, be at its peak, and right now you may be struggling to study even four hours.

category.main_topic: Finish the papers already chosen instead of postponing them
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Stop the 'later' escape
category.core_message: A smaller committed set of papers still has to be completed before anything new is added.
category.narrative_structure: deadline, the excuse, the reduced commitment, the repetition
category.hook: You defined the goal till December
category.takeaway: Execute the three papers before moving on
category.rationale: A goal-completion talk. The title matches.

transcript.original_text: आपका जो भी गोल है आपने वह डिफाइन कर लिया दिसंबर तक। इसको भूलना मत। देखो जैसे ही थोड़ा सा टफ होना शुरू होता है ना हमें लगता है बाद में देखेंगे। बाद में देखेंगे। प्लीज इसको भूलना मत। अगर आपने तीन पेपर भी लिखे हैं ना कि सर नहीं मैं तो सिर्फ जीएस टू, जीएस थ्री और ऑप्शनल पेपर वन करूंगा। बस मैं चौथा पेपर करूंगा ही नहीं। तो एटलीस्ट वो तीन पेपर फिर एक्सजीक्यूट होंगे। दे हैव टू बी एक्सजीक्यूटेड। दोज़ थ्री पेपर्स हैव टू गेट एक्सजीक्यूटेड। ओनली देन वी विल मूव ऑन टू द नेक्स्ट थिंग। कि हम अपने गोल्स को मीट करेंगे ही करेंगे। वी विल मीट आवर गोल्स। नो मैटर व्हाट हैपेंस। वी विल मीट आवर गोल्स।
transcript.english_translation: Whatever your goal is, you have defined it till December. Don't forget this. Look, as soon as it starts to get a little tough, we feel we'll see it later. We'll see it later. Please don't forget this. Even if you have written only three papers — 'sir, no, I will do only GS2, GS3, and optional paper 1. I just won't do the fourth paper' — then at least those three papers will be executed. They have to be executed. Those three papers have to get executed. Only then will we move on to the next thing. We will meet our goals, we will. We will meet our goals. No matter what happens. We will meet our goals.

transcript.original_text: एक बहुत ही क्रेजी चीज दिखाऊं आपको। बहुत ही क्रेजी। ठीक है? मतलब ये देखो ये ना एक गेम की वीडियो है। इस गेम का नाम है नाइट ऑफ बुश कैप्चर। इसमें यू एक्चुअली प्ले एज अलकायदा टेररिस्ट। इसमें आपका काम है अमेरिकनंस को मारना और फिर जाके फाइनली प्रेसिडेंट बुश को कैप्चर करना। एंड दिस वाज़ अ प्रोपोगेंडा मशीन मेड बाय अलकायदा कि यार हम प्रोपोगेंडा करेंगे और इस प्रोपोगेंडा के थ्रू लोग हमसे इंस्पायर्ड होंगे। सो दे हैव एक्चुअली डन दिस। इट कैन बी रिटन एस एन एग्जांपल ऑफ टेक फॉर प्रोपोगेंडा।
transcript.english_translation: Let me show you a very crazy thing. Very crazy. Okay? I mean, look, this is a video of a game. The name of this game is Knights of Bush Capture. In this you actually play as an Al-Qaeda terrorist. Your job in this is to kill Americans and then finally go and capture President Bush. And this was a propaganda machine made by Al-Qaeda, that we will do propaganda and through this propaganda people will be inspired by us. So they have actually done this. It can be written as an example of tech for propaganda. [The game title is given as captioned. I did not verify the title against a store page.]

shorts.style_interpretation: Observed template family: rounded_card_title_header. Title as read: How Terrorists Turned a Video Game Into Propaganda. The 1fps sample counted 7 primary-teacher frames, 14 overlay frames, and 8 frames where B-roll hid the teacher, out of 29 sampled frames. These counts describe the sample. They are not a claim about the editor's intention. Direct observations are the timeline rows. Any reason a B-roll insert was chosen is a hypothesis tied to the spoken phrase in that row.

category.main_topic: Trafficking of women and children, and an argument for special protection
subtopics: internal routes toward Delhi, Haryana, Punjab
cross-border claims about Bangladesh and Nepal
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Connect a crime pattern to special legal protection
category.core_message: He describes trafficking as something that happens to women and children and says he supports reservation and extra protection. Several phrases in the caption are rough.
category.narrative_structure: routes, a show, then the policy line
category.hook: A cross-border sentence opens the caption
category.takeaway: He supports special protection because of who the victims are

category.rationale: Sensitive claims are reported as the speaker's words. The caption is rough enough that names and purposes should be checked before reuse.

transcript.original_text: बांग्लादेशी वुमेन मेनली फॉर डोमेस्टिक [संगीत] वर्क एंड नेपाली वुमेन फॉर सेक्स वर्क। इंडिया में इंटरनल ट्रैफिकिंग हो रही है। इस पे शोज़ भी बने हैं। राइट? अगर आप देखना चाहो दिल्ली क्राइम देख सकते हो आप। उसमें यही चीज दिखाई गई है कि नॉर्थ [संगीत] ईस्ट से वुमेन को उठा के लाइक चिल्ड्रन आर सोल्ड और वुमेन आर पिक्ड अप एंड देन दे आर ब्रॉट टू दिल्ली, हरियाणा, पंजाब एंड इन दीज़ एरियाज़ दे आर फोर्स्ड इनू फोर्स मैरिजेस एंड प्रॉस्टिट्यूशन। तो एक इंटरनल ट्रैफिकिंग का इशू है कि अपनी कंट्री में यहां से वहां जा रहे हैं। एक ट्रैफिकिंग का इशू क्रॉस बॉर्डर ट्रैफिकिंग का है। बांग्लादेशी वुमेन मेनली फॉर डोमेस्टिक [संगीत] वर्क एंड नेपाली वुमेन फॉर सेक्स वर्क आर बीइंग टेकन इंटू द कंट्री। आई एम फेयरली इन फेवर ऑफ़ वुमेस रिजर्वेशन एंड गिविंग देम स्पेशल प्रोटेक्शन एक्सेट्रा। तो कई लोग कहते हैं कि नहीं यह बनता नहीं है एक्सेट्रा। यह वुमेन को स्पेशल प्रिविलेजेस क्यों देनी है वगैरह-वगैरह। यह तो इक्वल है। दिस नेवर हैपेंस टू अ मैन। इट ओनली है हपेंस टू वीमेन एंड चिल्ड्रन। एंड द क्राइम इज एफिडेबली डन बाई अ मैन।
transcript.english_translation: Bangladeshi women mainly for domestic work, and Nepali women for sex work. Internal trafficking is happening in India. Shows have been made on this. Right? If you want to watch, you can watch Delhi Crime. In that, this very thing has been shown: women are picked up from the Northeast, like children are sold, and women are picked up and then they are brought to Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, and in these areas they are forced into forced marriages and prostitution. So there is an issue of internal trafficking, that within our own country they are going from here to there. There is one trafficking issue of cross-border trafficking. Bangladeshi women mainly for domestic work and Nepali women for sex work are being taken into the country. I am fairly in favour of women's reservation and of giving them special protection, extra. So many people say, no, this is not acceptable, extra, why give women special privileges, and so on. This is equality. This never happens to a man. It only happens to women and children. And the crime is affordably done by a man. [The last clause is captioned 'affordably' and is probably a mishearing. It is left marked rather than replaced. The Northeast, Delhi Crime, and the cross-border sentence are in the caption.]

category.main_topic: Ethanol blending and the sugar shortage he attributes to it
subtopics: first extra sugar import in nine years
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Show the other side of an ethanol policy
category.core_message: The stated benefits are cheaper petrol, less pollution, less oil import, and farmer income. The stated cost is sugar diverted into a fuel that he says pays more than petrol.
category.narrative_structure: policy benefits, then the flip side
category.hook: India is about to import extra sugar
category.takeaway: A decision has a consequence on the other side
category.entities: ethanol; petrol; sugarcane; Diwali; Dussehra; 72 rupees
category.rationale: Figures and the import claim are the speaker's.

transcript.original_text: एंड फॉर द फर्स्ट टाइम इन नाइन इयर्स इन दी अपकमिंग फेस्टिव सीज़न फॉर दिवाली दशहरा एक्सेट्रा इंडिया इज़ गोइंग टू इंपोर्ट शुगर। व्हाट डीड आवर गवर्नमेंट डू? आर गवर्नमेंट सेड वी आर गोइंग टू कन्वर्ट शुगर केन इंटू एथेनॉल। तो हम इसे पेट्रोल में मिक्स करेंगे। पेट्रोल विल बिकम चीपर। देयर विल बी लेसर पोलुशन। वी विल हैव टू इंपोर्ट लेस ऑफ़ पेट्रोल। वी विल सेव आवर फॉरेन एक्सचेंज। एंड वी हैव एक्सेस शुगर केन प्रोडक्शन एनीवे। एंड सिंस देयर इज़ एक्सेस शुगरकेन प्रोडक्शन फार्मर्स विल गेट मोर मनी। कोई भी डिसीजन आप लेते हो उस डिसीजन का आप एक फ्लिप साइड कॉन्सक्वेंस भी सोचो। एक्चुअली एथेनॉल पेज़ अराउंड ₹72 पर लीटर। ठीक है? इट इज मच मोर एक्सपेंसिव देन पेट्रोल। फार्मर कह रहा है यार मैं फूड क्यों उगाऊं? लेट मी जस्ट पुट दिस मनी इनटू एथेनॉल। नाउ वी हैव अ सिचुएशन वेयर देयर इज अ शुगर शॉर्टेज बिकॉज़ ऑफ दिस डायवर्जन।
transcript.english_translation: And for the first time in nine years, in the upcoming festive season, for Diwali and Dussehra, India is going to import extra sugar. What did our government do? Our government said we are going to convert sugarcane into ethanol. So we will mix it into petrol. Petrol will become cheaper. There will be less pollution. We will have to import less petrol. We will save our foreign exchange. And we have excess sugarcane production anyway. And since there is excess sugarcane production, farmers will get more money. Whatever decision you take, also think of a flip-side consequence of that decision. Actually ethanol pays around 72 rupees per litre. Okay? It is much more expensive than petrol. The farmer is saying, why should I grow food? Let me just put this money into ethanol. Now we have a situation where there is a sugar shortage because of this diversion.

metadata.title: Why India Couldn't Stop the Kandahar Hijack
metadata.user_topic_description: (WHY INDIA COULDNT STOP THE KANDAHAR)
metadata.description: Why India Couldn't Stop the Kandahar Hijack

category.main_topic: The Kandahar hijack as a failure of a pre-set response
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Use the hijack to argue for decisions made before the crisis
category.core_message: He says the plane could have been stopped in India and was not, because the response was being invented after the hijack.
category.narrative_structure: narrative, then the lesson
category.hook: The hijacked plane sat at an Indian airport for two hours
category.takeaway: Crisis response has to be settled in advance
category.rationale: A history-to-lesson short.

transcript.original_text: IC814 दिस वाज़ एन इंडियन एयरलाइंस प्लेन। यह प्लेन हाईजैक होने के बाद जो टेररिस्ट जिन्होंने इसको हाईजैक किया था वो इसको कांदा ले जाना चाहते थे अफगानिस्तान में। प्लेन में फ्यूल कम था। प्लेन इंडिया में लैंड हुआ। 2 घंटे के लिए प्लेन इंडियन एयरपोर्ट पे खड़ा रहा। बट क्योंकि हमारा कोऑर्डिनेशन सॉर्टेड नहीं था। हमने प्लेन को स्टॉर्म नहीं किया। हमने रिफ्यूल करने दिया। प्लेन कांदा चला गया। वो जो होस्टेजेस थे उनको फ्री कराने के लिए हमें चारप टेररिस्ट को रिलीज करना पड़ा। अगर यह क्राइसिस के बाद शुरू होता है कि हाईजैकिंग हो गई। अब बताओ क्या करना है? तो डिले होता है, डेफिशिएंसी आती है। तो इस टाइप की स्ट्रेटेजिक [संगीत] मिस्टेक्स होती है। सो द फैक्ट इज़ दैट दिस प्राइसेस रिस्पांस मस्ट बी सेटल्ड [संगीत] इन एडवांस।
transcript.english_translation: IC 814. This was an Indian Airlines plane. After this plane was hijacked, the terrorists who had hijacked it wanted to take it to Kandahar in Afghanistan. The plane was low on fuel. The plane landed in India. For two hours the plane stood at an Indian airport. But because our coordination was not sorted, we did not storm the plane. We allowed it to refuel. The plane went to Kandahar. To free the hostages that were there, we had to release four terrorists. If, after a crisis starts — the hijacking has happened, now say what to do — then there is delay, deficiency comes in. So these types of strategic mistakes happen. So the fact is that this crisis response must be settled in advance. [The caption says 'four-ish' terrorists in one phonetic spelling and the number is translated as four.]

category.main_topic: The state's legal monopoly of violence
subtopics: peaceful protest as the exception he states
category.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants, inferred from the channel and the speech
category.purpose: Define a political-theory idea in plain language
category.core_message: He says only the state may use violence under law, and a private person using violence is challenging that authority.
category.narrative_structure: repetition of the contrast, then the limit
category.hook: If I kill someone it is illegitimate
category.takeaway: The legal power sits with the state, and he excludes a peaceful protest
category.rationale: A concept explainer. The title's provocation is the speech's actual claim.

transcript.original_text: मैं अगर किसी को मार दूं तो इललेजिटमेट है। किसी भी कंट्री में वायलेंस का एक्सक्लूसिव राइट गवर्नमेंट के पास होता है। मैं अगर किसी को मार दूं तो इललेजिटिमेट है। बट स्टेट मार सकता है। दैट इज द पावर ऑफ द स्टेट। इट इज द ओनली एंटिटी इन आवर डेमोक्रेसी जो वायलेंस कर सकती है एस पर लॉ। मैं किसी पे गोली नहीं चला सकता। बट स्टेट चला सकता है। मैं किसी को लाठी से नहीं मार सकता। क्राइम है बट स्टेट मार सकता है। लॉ में लिखा है कि स्टेट मार सकता है। ऑफ कोर्स नॉट ऑन अ पीसफुल प्रोटेस्ट बट जब कोई वायलेंट हो जाए। व्हेन समबडी एल्स स्टार्ट्स एक्सरसाइजिंग दैट वायलेंस दे आर चैलेंजिंग द अथॉरिटी ऑफ दिस गवर्नमेंट।
transcript.english_translation: If I kill someone, it is illegitimate. In any country, the exclusive right to violence is with the government. If I kill someone, it is illegitimate. But the state can kill. That is the power of the state. It is the only entity in our democracy that can do violence as per law. I cannot shoot someone. But the state can. I cannot hit someone with a stick. That is a crime, but the state can hit. It is written in the law that the state can kill. Of course not at a peaceful protest, but when someone becomes violent. When somebody else starts exercising that violence, they are challenging the authority of this government.

transcript.original_text: भाई लेक्चर है। Netflix की सीरीज नहीं है। ऐसा मत करो कि सुबह उठे आज मैं चार लेक्चर देखूंगा। एक लेक्चर कंप्लीट किया, आधे घंटे का ब्रेक, फिर एक लेक्चर कंप्लीट किया, फिर आधे घंटे का ब्रेक। फिर एक लेक्चर कंप्लीट किया और मैंने तो आज बहुत पढ़ाई कर ली। दिस इज नॉट हाउ इट्स सपोज टू बी डन। सो व्हाट इज सपोज टू बी डन? आपका गोल होना चाहिए कि मान लो आपने कोई लेक्चर देखा। उसके साथ आपने कुछ नोट्स बनाए या आपको कुछ पीडीएफ नोट्स मिले हुए हैं। लेक्चर को बंद करो। उन नोट्स को भी बंद करो और एक ब्लैंक पेपर पे लिखो कि मुझे इस लेक्चर से क्या समझ आया। काफी गैप्स होंगे इसमें। ऐसा नहीं है कि आप एक बारी में सब कुछ रिप्रोड्यूस कर दोगे। नहीं कर पाओ। बट जब यहां पर गैप्स दिखेंगे तो आपको रियलाइज होगा व्हाट यू अंडरस्टुड एंड व्हाट यू डिड नॉट। उसके बाद जाके ये नोट्स पढ़ो और फिर अपने गैप्स को एनालाइज करो।
transcript.english_translation: Brother, a lecture is a lecture. It is not a Netflix series. Don't do this: you wake up in the morning, today I will watch four lectures. Finished one lecture, a half-hour break, then finished one lecture, then a half-hour break, then finished one lecture, and I studied a lot today. This is not how it's supposed to be done. So what is supposed to be done? Your goal should be: suppose you watched some lecture. Along with it you made some notes, or you have received some PDF notes. Close the lecture. Close those notes too, and on a blank paper write what you understood from this lecture. There will be quite a few gaps in this. It is not that you will reproduce everything in one go. You won't be able to. But when the gaps show up here, you will realise what you understood and what you did not. After that, read these notes, and then analyse your gaps.
